plan.goal: Build a playable Minecraft-like MVP in the browser with React 18, three.js and Vite. The pure ESM engine in src/engine/ must meet the full contract and pass `node --test`. The React/three UI must provide a menu, an infinite seeded world, mining, building, an inventory, crafting, a day/night cycle, saving and a polished HUD. All textures are generated in code.

steps.step: Implement blocks.js to the spec: fixed id constants for blocks 0-14 and items 100-103, plus getBlock, getItem, isSolid and isTransparent. getBlock and getItem throw RangeError for unknown ids. Hardness is Infinity for water and bedrock. maxStack is 1 for pickaxes and 64 for everything else. Implement daynight.js: DAY_LENGTH=1200 and skyState with t wrapping to [0,1) for negative seconds and continuous daylight in [0.15,1]. Add a pure src/engine/atlasLayout.js that exports ATLAS_TILES (the grid size) and tileFor(blockId, faceDir). It gives each block a tile index and separate tiles for grass top/side/bottom, log top/side and the crafting-table faces. It also exports tileUV(tile) returning a u0,v0,u1,v1 rectangle inside [0,1].

Implement noise.js. hashSeed takes a string or number and returns a uint32 (FNV/murmur-style mixing, so 'abc' and 'abd' differ). createRng is a seeded PRNG such as mulberry32 that returns values in [0,1). createNoise2D is seeded gradient/simplex noise clamped to [-1,1] and continuous, so points 0.01 apart differ by less than 0.05. Different seeds must give different fields. No external dependencies.

Implement the pure modules inventory.js, crafting.js and mining.js to the spec, importing the ids and getItem/getBlock from blocks.js. Inventory: addItem fills existing stacks first, then empty slots, and returns leftover. removeFromSlot, selectSlot (RangeError outside 0-8), scrollSelection with wrap-around, moveStack (move/merge/swap) and selectedItem are all included. Crafting: accept only 2x2 or 3x3 grids and match on the bounding box of non-null cells so shaped recipes may be shifted. The pickaxes are 3x3 only. Shapeless recipes are log and sand+coal. Any extra item invalidates a recipe. consumeIngredients is pure. Mining: canHarvest, breakTime with the tool-speed formula (Infinity for unbreakable blocks), and dropsFor. No argument may ever be mutated.

Implement world.js. chunkIndex. generateChunk uses height h(x,z) from world-coordinate noise, clamped to [SEA_LEVEL-8, SEA_LEVEL+20] so there are no seams. It places a bedrock floor, grass/sand top, 3 dirt/sand layers, stone, water up to SEA_LEVEL, and ores from a per-chunk RNG (coal y≤40 with at least one guaranteed per chunk, iron y≤24). Trees go on grass with trunks at local 2..13, 4-6 logs high, and leaves only where the cell was air, never outside the chunk. createWorld(seed,{flat}) keeps a chunk cache and an edits Map. getBlockAt handles negative coordinates with floor division, returns BEDROCK below y=0 and AIR at y≥64. setBlockAt throws RangeError outside [0,63], records the edit, and deletes the edit when a block is reverted to its generated value. Also implement getSurfaceHeight, serializeWorld (edits sorted by x,y,z, exact JSON key order) and deserializeWorld (throws Error on version≠1, round-trips byte-identically). Expose a chunk-version or dirty counter on the world so the renderer can tell when to remesh.

Create the procedural texture module src/render/textures.js. It draws 16x16 pixel-art tiles on a canvas following atlasLayout (grass top/side/bottom, log rings/bark, ores, glass, leaves with alpha holes, water, planks, crafting table, and item icons for stick, pickaxes and coal). It also makes 10 crack-stage textures. Export: a THREE.CanvasTexture atlas with NearestFilter and no mipmaps; a crack texture array; and iconDataURL(itemId) for use in the HUD and inventory.

Build the React UI components and styles from props and callbacks only, with no game-loop logic. MainMenu: title, seed field with a random default, a render-distance slider 2-8 (default 4), 'Novo mundo', and 'Continuar' shown only if a save exists. Hud: crosshair, hotbar with icons and counts, item name shown for 2 s on slot change, underwater tint. InventoryScreen: 36 slots plus a 2x2 or 3x3 crafting grid and result slot, with click to pick up and put down stacks via a cursor stack, using engine moveStack/craft/consumeIngredients. PauseMenu: Continue, Save, Quit to menu. DebugOverlay: FPS, XYZ, chunk, facing, targeted block, seed, time of day.

Implement mesher.js buildChunkMesh(world,cx,cz) → {opaque, transparent} as typed arrays. Emit 4 vertices and 6 indices per face, with world-space positions, outward normals, counter-clockwise winding seen from outside, and UVs from atlasLayout.tileUV. A face is emitted only when the neighbor is AIR or is transparent with a different id. Neighbors in other chunks are read through getBlockAt, with BEDROCK below y=0 and AIR above y=63. WATER, GLASS and LEAVES go to transparent. Read the chunk array directly for speed where possible.

Implement raycast.js and physics.js. Raycast: Amanatides-Woo DDA with unnormalized direction, skipping AIR and WATER. It returns {x,y,z,block,face,distance}, where distance is to the entry point. If the origin is inside a solid block it returns that block with face [0,0,0] and distance 0. It returns null beyond maxDistance. Physics: the constants table, createPlayer and collidesAt. canPlaceBlock is false when the block cube intersects the player's AABB. stepPlayer is pure: substeps of ≤0.05 s; yaw-based direction with normalized diagonals; direct speed for walk/sprint/sneak; gravity clamped to terminal velocity; jump only onGround; AABB collision resolved on Y, then X, then Z, with feet snapped to block tops and upward velocity zeroed at ceilings. It also covers sneak edge protection, water rules (1/4 gravity, sink at most 3 blocks/s, swim up at 3 blocks/s) and flying.

Add the three.js render layer. ChunkRenderer loads and unloads chunks around the player within render distance, meshes a few chunks per frame nearest-first, remeshes edited chunks and their neighbors, and disposes geometry. It uses an opaque material plus a transparent material: water semi-transparent, leaves and glass alpha-tested. Sky: background color from skyState, sun and moon sprites, ambient and directional light driven by daylight, fog at the render-distance edge. Selection: wireframe outline of the targeted block plus a crack overlay box showing mining progress.

Wire the game end to end. Input controller: pointer lock, mouse look with pitch clamped to ±89°, WASD, Space, Shift, Ctrl or double-tap W to sprint, F to fly, 1-9 and wheel for the hotbar, E/Esc/F3, mouse buttons. Save module: localStorage key mc-mvp-save storing world, player position/yaw/pitch, inventory and time. Game.jsx: three scene, camera at eye height, RAF loop calling stepPlayer, raycast within 5 blocks, timed mining via breakTime with reset on release or target change and drops into the inventory, placement with canPlaceBlock that consumes 1 item, right-click on a crafting table to open 3x3 crafting, middle-click pick-block, day clock, autosave every 30 s and on pause, spawn at the world center on getSurfaceHeight+1. App.jsx switches between menu and game, including Continue. Replace main.jsx so it renders App and imports the styles.

doneWhen: `npm test` passes, including hidden contract tests on edge cases (negative coords, RangeErrors, purity, serialize round-trip, culling rules, DDA inside-block case).
`npm run build` completes with no errors and src/engine imports no three, react or DOM APIs.
`npm run dev` shows the main menu with seed, render-distance slider, Novo mundo, and Continuar only when a save exists.
In game: infinite seeded terrain with trees, water and ores streams around the player without stutter, with sky, sun/moon, lighting and fog following the day cycle.
Mining with crack progress, placing, inventory (E), 2x2 and crafting-table 3x3 crafting, hotbar with icons and the item name shown for 2 s, F3 debug, flying, swimming and sneaking all work.
Autosave every 30 s and on pause to localStorage `mc-mvp-save`, and Continuar restores the world edits, player pose, inventory and time.
About 60 fps at render distance 4 with no console errors.
risks: Parallel steps depend on contracts they cannot run yet: physics, raycast and the mesher depend on world.js; mining, crafting and the mesher depend on blocks.js and atlasLayout. Implementers must follow the spec signatures exactly.
Seamless terrain: height must be computed from world coordinates, and tree, ore and the guaranteed-coal placement must be deterministic per chunk while keeping leaves inside the chunk.
Physics edge cases are tricky to get right (exact foot snapping, step-up limit of 1 block, sneak edge stop, water and flying substeps).
Performance: meshing on the main thread must be budgeted per frame, and old geometry must be disposed to avoid leaks and frame drops.
serializeWorld must keep the exact key order and edit sort order so the round-trip is byte-identical, and reverting a block must remove its edit.
Transparent rendering order and depth issues between water, glass and leaves, and between the crack overlay and blocks.

notes: Atlas contract gap (steps 1, 5, 6, 7): atlasLayout only defines tileFor(blockId, faceDir), but textures.js must also draw the icons for STICK, WOODEN_PICKAXE, STONE_PICKAXE and COAL. Add an item-tile mapping to atlasLayout (e.g. tileForItem(id)). Also fix the V orientation in one place: state whether tile row 0 is the top of the canvas and whether the CanvasTexture uses flipY, so the mesher UVs, the canvas drawing and iconDataURL agree. Keep the UVs strictly inside [0,1] and inside the tile. Fix the faceDir encoding (normal array or index 0-5) in step 1, because the mesher and the textures are written in parallel waves.

world.js internal contract (steps 4, 7, 9): define explicitly how edits and the chunk cache coexist. Recommended: the cached chunk array has the edits applied, and setBlockAt compares against the pristine generated value (kept or regenerated) so that reverting deletes the edit. The edits Map key must work for negative coordinates. Document the fields the mesher and renderer may read (chunk getter, per-chunk version). These fields must not leak into serializeWorld, which has to stay byte-identical on round-trip. Meshing reads neighbors through getBlockAt, which generates and caches the adjacent chunks, so add a way to evict cached chunks far from the player (edits are kept) or the 'infinite' world leaks memory.

Inventory screen item loss (steps 6, 10): specify that closing the inventory or crafting screen (E, Esc, or the pause opening) returns the cursor stack and everything in the crafting grid to the inventory through addItem. Taking the result must check that it fits (in the cursor or the inventory) before calling consumeIngredients. Decide who owns the inventory state: Game owns it, the screen gets it by props and callbacks, and the grid and cursor are local to the screen. Mining drops with leftover > 0 must not crash.

Pointer lock and browser key handling (step 10): while the pointer is locked, the browser consumes Esc and the keydown is not reliable. Drive the pause from the `pointerlockchange` event (lock lost with no other screen open means pause plus save). Catch the rejection of requestPointerLock, since re-locking shortly after Esc throws and would break the 'no console errors' criterion. Call preventDefault on F3, on contextmenu (right click), on the middle-click auto-scroll and on wheel. Opening E or the crafting table must exit pointer lock without triggering the pause. Ignore game input while any screen is open, and clear held keys on blur and on lock loss.

Game loop and React boundary (step 10, perf criterion): keep the player, the inventory mirror, the clock and the mining progress in refs or a plain game object updated in the RAF loop. Push to React state only on change or throttled (HUD and debug at most ~4-10 Hz, inventory on mutation). Never call setState every frame. Clamp the frame dt (e.g. ≤0.1 s) before stepPlayer. Dispose the renderer, geometries, textures and listeners on unmount (Sair para o menu), which also keeps React 18 StrictMode double-mount safe. On Continuar, restore `flying` together with position, yaw and pitch, and pass the render distance from the menu into ChunkRenderer and the fog.

sessions.summary:
Step 1 (wave 1) is implemented in the three files it names. Shell access was partly denied, so I could only run `npm test`, not `npm run build` or ad-hoc node checks.

**Files written**
- `src/engine/blocks.js`: ids 0–14 and items 100–103 as exports; `getBlock`, `getItem`, `isSolid`, `isTransparent`. Unknown or non-integer ids throw `RangeError`. Hardness is `Infinity` for water and bedrock. `maxStack` is 1 for pickaxes and 64 otherwise. `placeable` is false for AIR, WATER and all items. Each call returns a new object.
- `src/engine/daynight.js`: `DAY_LENGTH = 1200` and `skyState`. `t` is wrapped to [0,1) including negatives. `daylight = 0.15 + 0.85·(0.5 + 0.5·sin(2πt))`, clamped to [0.15, 1]. `isNight` is `t > 0.5 && t < 1`.
- `src/engine/atlasLayout.js` (new): the atlas contract, which the other steps depend on.
  - Grid is `ATLAS_TILES = 8` (64 tiles), `TILE_PX = 16`, `ATLAS_PX = 128`.
  - V convention: tile row 0 is the top of the canvas. The texture must use `flipY = false`, so `v = 0` is the canvas top. `tileUV` returns `v0` at the top of the tile and `v1` at the base.
  - Face encoding: index 0..5 = +X, −X, +Y (top), −Y (bottom), +Z, −Z. `FACE_NORMALS` is exported. `tileFor` also accepts a normal array.
  - `tileFor(blockId, faceDir)`: AIR returns −1, unknown ids throw `RangeError`.
  - `tileForItem(itemId)`: maps items 100–103 to their icon tiles. Block ids return their top-face tile.
  - `tileUV(tile)`: returns `{u0,v0,u1,v1}` inside the tile, inset by half a texel.
  - `TILE` exports the named indices, from GRASS_TOP (0) through COAL (22).

**Verification**
- `npm test`: the blocks, daynight and mining-related tests pass, along with the inventory test. The 6 failures are in other steps' stubs (world, noise, crafting, raycast, physics). They are not in my files.
- I did not run `npm run build`.
- `atlasLayout.js` has no test; I checked it by reading only.

Implemented noise.js (FNV+murmur hashSeed, mulberry32 createRng, seeded Perlin createNoise2D clamped to [-1,1]) and inventory.js, crafting.js, mining.js (pure, per contract). Visible tests for noise, inventory, crafting, mining and daynight pass. The 5 remaining npm test failures are world, mesher, raycast and physics, which belong to later waves. I did not run npm run build.

I wrote steps 4–6 (`src/render/textures.js`, the five `src/ui/*.jsx` components and `src/ui/styles.css`). I ran `npm run build` and it passes. I did not run `npm test`, and none of the new files have been run or even loaded. `main.jsx` doesn't import them until the wiring wave, so the build never compiled them.

- **`src/render/textures.js`**:
  - It draws the atlas, one 16x16 tile per `TILE` entry, using the layout and V convention from `atlasLayout`. The texture uses `NearestFilter`, no mipmaps and `flipY=false`.
  - It exports `getAtlasCanvas`, `getAtlasTexture`, `getCrackTextures` (10 stages), `iconDataURL(itemId)` (via `tileForItem`, so blocks show their top tile) and `disposeTextures`.
- **`src/ui`**:
  - **`MainMenu`** has the seed field with a random default, a render-distance slider (2–8, default 4), "Novo mundo", and "Continuar" only when `hasSave` is true. It calls `onNewWorld({seed, renderDistance})` and `onContinue({renderDistance})`.
  - **`Hud`** has the crosshair, the hotbar with icons and counts, the item name for 2 s on a slot or item change, and the underwater tint. It also exports `ItemIcon`.
  - **`PauseMenu`** has Continue, Save and Quit to menu.
  - **`DebugOverlay`** takes an `info` object with fps, position, chunk, facing, target, seed and time.
  - **`styles.css`** styles all of the above.
- **`InventoryScreen`** (follows the review notes):
  - Game owns the inventory and passes it in with `onChange`. The crafting grid (2x2 or 3x3 via `gridSize`) and the cursor stack are local to the screen.
  - Clicking picks up, puts down, merges and swaps stacks. Right-click takes half or places one.
  - Taking the result checks that it fits in the cursor before calling `consumeIngredients`.
  - Closing or unmounting the screen (E, Esc, pause) returns the cursor and grid contents to the inventory through `addItem`, and it is safe under StrictMode. Anything that doesn't fit in a full inventory is discarded.

I implemented steps 7–8 in `src/engine/mesher.js`, `src/engine/raycast.js` and `src/engine/physics.js`, but none of it has been run against a real world. `src/engine/world.js` is still the stub from the skeleton (`createWorld` and `generateChunk` throw "não implementado"), so the mesher, raycast and physics tests fail on that. `npm test` shows 6 of 11 passing, and the 5 failures all come from `world.js`. `npm run build` succeeds.

- **Mesher:** `buildChunkMesh` follows the culling rule in the spec. UVs come from `tileUV` and `tileFor`. I checked the counter-clockwise winding on paper only. It reads every neighbour through `getBlockAt`, so it does not depend on how `world.js` stores chunks.
- **Raycast:** Amanatides–Woo DDA with the direction normalized internally, skipping `AIR` and `WATER`. It returns the origin block with `face: [0,0,0]` and `distance: 0` when the origin is inside a solid block, and `null` past `maxDistance`.
- **Physics:**
  - Constants, `createPlayer`, `collidesAt` and `canPlaceBlock` follow the spec.
  - `stepPlayer` is pure and splits `dt` into substeps of at most 0.05 s.
  - It resolves collisions on Y, then X, then Z, in moves of at most 0.5 blocks, so terminal-velocity falls cannot tunnel through blocks.
  - It also covers sneak edge protection, the water rules and flying.
  - When flying, `sneak` descends at walk speed instead of slowing horizontal movement.

Once `world.js` lands, `npm test` should be re-run to confirm the mesher, raycast and physics tests pass.

I added `src/render/ChunkRenderer.js`, `src/render/Sky.js` and `src/render/Selection.js`. `npm run build` passes, but nothing imports these files yet, so the build doesn't exercise them. I did not run `npm test` and did not run the game in a browser, so none of it has been exercised. `world.js` was still a stub in the working tree, so none of the render code has been run against a real world.

- **ChunkRenderer:**
  - It takes `(scene, world, atlasTexture, renderDistance)`.
  - `update(px, pz, budget)` remeshes edited chunks first (up to 4 per frame) and unloads chunks beyond renderDistance+1. It then meshes up to `budget` new chunks per frame, nearest first, and returns how many are still missing.
  - It calls `world.evictChunk?.(cx, cz)` on unload, so the world needs to provide that method for memory to be freed. It is optional here and does nothing if `world.js` doesn't have it.
  - `markBlockChanged(x, y, z)` marks the chunk and any border neighbours for remeshing. Game must call it after every `setBlockAt`, because the renderer tracks edits itself and does not read a chunk version from the world.
  - Opaque and transparent meshes use separate materials. The transparent one is alpha-tested at 0.05 so leaves and glass are cut out, and water uses the texture's own alpha.
  - `isReady(px, pz)` and `dispose()` are also there.
- **Sky:**
  - `new Sky(scene, renderDistance)`; `update(seconds, camera)` returns the `skyState`.
  - Sky colour and fog colour follow the day, with an orange tint near sunrise and sunset.
  - Ambient and directional light follow `daylight`, the sun and moon are sprites around the camera, and fog sits at the render-distance edge.
  - `setRenderDistance` and `dispose` are included.
- **Selection:**
  - `new Selection(scene)`; `update({x, y, z} | null, progress)` draws a black wireframe on the targeted block.
  - With `progress > 0` it also shows a crack overlay box using the matching one of the 10 crack textures.
  - `dispose()` is included.

Wrote src/game/input.js, save.js, Game.jsx, src/App.jsx and src/main.jsx. `npm run build` passes. `npm test` fails 5 of 11 tests, all because src/engine/world.js is still the stub from the skeleton (it throws 'não implementado' from generateChunk/createWorld), which belongs to another step; the same stub blocks the mesher, raycast and physics tests. I could not play the game in a browser, so the game wiring has not been run. It covers: pointer-lock/pause handling, mining with cracks, placing, pick-block, crafting-table and inventory screens, 30 s autosave plus save on pause and quit, Continue restoring pose/flying/inventory/time, throttled React state, and cleanup on unmount.
